subject: Seller entity declaration & VAT ID proof for cross-border invoice netting
messages:
From: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@indotrade.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T08:15:00Z
Subject: VAT status and netting for May invoice

Hi Markus,

We received the May invoices from Redwood for our marketplace fees. Our accounts team is preparing a netting request against platform credits but they flagged your invoice for missing seller VAT declarations. Can you confirm the seller entity country and whether the reverse-charge applies here? Also we need a VAT certificate for FinServe (recipient) to support zero-rating where applicable.

Requested:
- Seller entity (country / EU VAT registration)
- Whether supply is B2B digital service or marketplace fee (we currently treat as platform service)
- VAT certificate or evidence for FinServe to support the claim

We are putting payment on hold until we get this. Please advise — Anita (FinServe AP)

--
Anita Sharma
Head of Accounts Payable
FinServe Ltd
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@finserve.co.uk>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT status and netting for May invoice

Hi Anita — thanks for the heads up. Looping in Laura and Priyom from finance/tax.

Short answer: Redwood invoiced platform fees from Redwood EU entity (Redwood Europe B.V.). For marketplace settlements to third-party sellers we may reverse-charge where seller is an EU VAT-registered business and place-of-supply is their member state. The May invoice you referenced is a platform fee billed to FinServe (B2B) and we expect reverse-charge treatment if FinServe is VAT-registered in the UK/EU.

Actions I will take now:
1) Share the seller entity declaration matrix we keep for marketplace settlements (attached)
2) Provide FinServe VAT certificate stub for your records (attaching what we have on file)
3) Priyom will confirm whether this invoice should be zero-rated or standard (depends on seller residency & nature of service)

I understand payment is on hold — we’ll get you the evidence ASAP.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): seller-declaration-matrix.csv (summary of seller entities), finserve_vat_certificate.pdf (copy provided by FinServe in onboarding)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@finserve.co.uk>
Date: 2026-05-22T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT status and netting for May invoice

Markus / Laura — brief update after reviewing the matrix and underlying seller declarations:

- Seller: Indotrade Solutions (third-party seller routed through our marketplace). Seller country: India (non-EU).
- Place of supply for platform fee: per EU VAT rules for electronically supplied services, the place of supply to a B2B customer is the customer's location (FinServe, UK).
- Reverse-charge applicability: For B2B where seller is non-EU, standard reverse-charge between EU supplier and UK business may not apply the same; however because Redwood billed from Redwood Europe B.V., we need to confirm whether the supply is considered outside the scope (place of supply = UK) and whether UK VAT should be charged.

Recommendation:
1) If FinServe can provide active UK VAT registration and a VAT certificate, they can self-account (reverse-charge) for the VAT due on the platform fee.
2) If not, Redwood may need to charge UK VAT on the invoice.

Action items: Laura, can you confirm whether we should reissue the invoice with UK VAT or provide a supplier note confirming place-of-supply?

Priyom
Senior Tax Analyst
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@finserve.co.uk>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT status and netting for May invoice

Hi Anita,

Thanks for your patience. I reviewed the seller declarations and the onboarding evidence. Attached is a one-page supplier confirmation that states: Redwood Europe B.V. invoiced platform fees from NL and place-of-supply to B2B customers is the customer member state (UK).

Next steps for FinServe to enable netting / zero-rate treatment:
- Please upload a copy of your UK VAT registration (VAT cert or HMRC confirmation) to the DocuSign link we provided so our AP can clear the hold. DocuSign link: https://docusign.example.com/claim/ABC-12345
- Once we receive the certificate we will update the invoice metadata and re-run netting. If for any reason you cannot provide VAT evidence, we will reissue the invoice with UK VAT and flag it for collection separately.

Attachment(s): supplier-place-of-supply-note.pdf

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@finserve.co.uk>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT status and netting for May invoice

Hi Laura / Markus —

Thanks — we uploaded the HMRC confirmation and a scanned VAT certificate to the DocuSign link just now (attachment: finserve_hmrc_confirmation.pdf). FinServe confirms they are UK VAT-registered and will self-account for the VAT on the platform fee.

Please confirm when the payment hold will be released and whether you will re-run the netting for May credits.

Best,
Anita Sharma
Head of Accounts Payable
FinServe Ltd
